sources.title: Debugging post-silicon fails in the IBM POWER8 bring-up lab
sources.venue_or_publication: IBM Journal of Research and Development
sources.what_it_covers: Techniques and mechanisms for post-silicon validation of the POWER8 processor, including detailed descriptions of several functional bugs found during bring-up and the debug processes used to identify root causes.
sources.why_relevant: Directly provides real silicon bring-up failure-and-recovery stories for a major microprocessor, including physical/functional interactions.
sources.verification_hint: Debugging post-silicon fails in the IBM POWER8 bring-up lab IBM J. Res. Dev

sources.title: Post-silicon validation: It's the unique fails that hurt you
sources.what_it_covers: Account of a particularly difficult intermittent post-silicon bug (SSEL) encountered during microprocessor bring-up at Sun, including failure characteristics, experiments, mitigation, fix, and root cause.
sources.why_relevant: Classic named post-silicon failure recovery story focused on hard-to-reproduce silicon issues beyond pure logic bugs.
sources.verification_hint: "Post-silicon validation: It's the unique fails that hurt you" Ahuja ITC 2009

sources.title: The circuit and physical design of the POWER4 microprocessor
sources.venue_or_publication: IBM Journal of Research and Development
sources.what_it_covers: Detailed account of POWER4 circuit/physical design methodology, clock distribution, power, integration, and timing challenges faced by the multi-site team and how they were met to achieve schedule and frequency goals.
sources.why_relevant: Owned set already has the companion microarchitecture paper; this is the circuit/physical companion that discusses design-closure aspects including clocking and timing.
sources.verification_hint: Warnock "circuit and physical design of the POWER4" IBM JRD 2002

sources.title: Clocking design and analysis for a 600-MHz Alpha microprocessor
sources.what_it_covers: Design and analysis of the clock distribution network for the Alpha 21264, including grid/H-tree hybrid, skew targets, power, and implementation challenges in a high-frequency design.
sources.why_relevant: Concrete physical-design/CTS war-story material from a landmark high-performance microprocessor known for aggressive clocking.
sources.verification_hint: "Clocking design and analysis for a 600-MHz Alpha microprocessor" JSSC 1998

sources.title: A Case Study – Crosstalk role in delaying full-chip closure
sources.what_it_covers: Real design case where a path met timing at block level but failed at full-chip due to crosstalk delta differences; describes diagnosis, metal-layer ECO fix, and verification of recovery.
sources.why_relevant: Named engineering postmortem of a classic full-chip timing-closure failure caused by crosstalk after physical integration.
sources.verification_hint: "A Case Study – Crosstalk role in delaying full-chip closure" eInfochips

sources.title: SMIC 55nm Tape-out Timing Issue: When Clean STA Reports Failed in Silicon
sources.what_it_covers: Post-silicon timing failure on a mixed-signal SoC where STA was clean at signoff; root cause traced to consecutive delay-cell clustering from CTS/optimization; ECO recovery and lessons.
sources.why_relevant: Explicit silicon-vs-signoff timing failure and recovery story involving CTS-related physical design decisions.
sources.verification_hint: SMIC 55nm Tape-out Timing Issue When Clean STA Reports Failed in Silicon VLSI Shuttle
